heading: Atlas scale and metadata coverage
claim_text: The reference contained 5,916,760 fibroblast-lineage cells associated with 4,818 sample labels and 848 study labels, and 2,239,277 endothelial-lineage cells associated with 3,553 sample labels and 748 study labels (Fig. 1A,B). Samples and studies could contribute to both lineage collections. These counts represent recorded labels rather than independently verified donors, because a harmonized cross-study donor identifier was unavailable. The atlas constituted the broad expression reference; clock training used a separately filtered subset.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Atlas scale and metadata coverage
claim_text: Original tissue metadata contained 39 observed labels per lineage, including categories such as ascites and carcinoma that do not constitute a clean anatomical classification. The tissue-like categories displayed in Fig. 1C–E instead derive from the terminal suffix of each Celltype label: twelve fibroblast and eleven endothelial suffixes, including pan. These suffixes describe annotation names and must not be interpreted as original tissue assignments. The full atlas also included disease-associated and incompletely specified samples, precluding a uniformly healthy-cohort description.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Hierarchical annotations and descriptive support
claim_text: Broad fibroblast annotations comprised Myfibro, eFibro, iFibro and qFibro. The endothelial-lineage collection retained ArtEC, CapEC, VenEC, EndoMT, MCs and LEC. These categories resolved into 32 and 38 detailed Celltype labels, respectively (Extended Data Fig. 1A,B). MCs was retained as a source-defined category within the endothelial-lineage collection; its inclusion does not imply that all cells in that collection are conventional endothelial cells. Original UMAP coordinates were preserved, with 160,000 stratified representative cells displayed per lineage. Full-source counts, expression summaries and composition denominators were not reduced to the plotted subset.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Hierarchical annotations and descriptive support
claim_text: Marker detection and expression summaries supported broad state-associated patterns (Fig. 1G,H), and signature means provided a complementary description of the annotated states (Fig. 1I,J). These summaries were derived from the same annotated atlas and therefore represent descriptive support rather than independent identity validation. PI16, LUM and IL33 were unavailable in the fibroblast feature universe and were omitted from the corresponding marker panels. Composition across stored age groups and annotation suffixes was calculated from pooled cells, retaining unknown ages (Fig. 1E,F; Extended Data Fig. 1C–F). These cell-weighted proportions were descriptive and were not included as clock features.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Retrospective annotation agreement
claim_text: A separate marker-combination analysis measured agreement with existing broad annotations (Extended Data Fig. 2). The figure-specific selected combination achieved GSE-equal top-signature concordance of 79.27% for fibroblasts (95% study-bootstrap confidence interval, 75.66–82.56%; 246 retained studies) and 64.27% for endothelial-lineage cells (58.63–68.85%; 208 retained studies). At the annotation-by-Leiden-cluster level, the highest signature agreed with the reference in 51 of 55 fibroblast records and 32 of 44 endothelial records. Discordant clusters were retained rather than relabeled to force agreement.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Retrospective annotation agreement
claim_text: These agreement estimates were retrospective. Reference annotations were marker-informed, and the retained studies had been inspected in earlier analyses; their designation as a source holdout did not establish a newly blinded accuracy test. Additional filtering-strategy figures preserved evaluations from 24 TISCH and 32 HUSCH datasets, comparing recorded Marker, DEG(only) and DEG(like) procedures against their corresponding reference labels (Supplementary Figs. 1,2). Together, the atlas and supporting analyses establish a heterogeneous stromal reference with explicit annotation and metadata limitations, rather than a donor-balanced population sample.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Clock overview and grouped model comparison
claim_text: TabulaStromal predicts recorded chronological age from expression aggregated within each sample and annotated cell state, producing Celltype_Gene features (Fig. 2A). Explicit cell-type proportions or ratios were excluded. The development sets contained 640 fibroblast samples assigned to 634 conservative GSE/GSM proxy groups and 437 endothelial samples assigned to 431 groups. Grouped five-fold cross-validation compared thirteen model families at requested feature counts of 8,000, 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000. Each lineage had all 260 model–feature-count–fold combinations. Proxy groups were disjoint within saved training/validation splits, although unresolved cross-study donor reuse could not be excluded.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Clock overview and grouped model comparison
claim_text: Across the full benchmark, fibroblast XGBoost at 20,000 features ranked first by mean validation R², achieving 0.803 ± 0.020 with MAE 9.71 ± 0.66 years. Endothelial ExtraTrees at 20,000 features ranked first with R² 0.716 ± 0.116 and MAE 11.54 ± 1.84 years (mean ± sample standard deviation across five folds). These are descriptive model rankings; no paired superiority test established that either configuration outperformed every alternative. The three IDEAL-Age-inspired implementations were local variants, and their results do not constitute reproduction of the published immune-aging model [9].
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Clock overview and grouped model comparison
claim_text: The heatmaps in Fig. 2B–D present a different summary: source fold 4, with feature count selected for each model using that fold's validation result. They contain training, validation and FT30→ALL100 external values and are neither five-fold means nor a benchmark of the later compact models. Moreover, MAD in panel D is the mean absolute deviation of observed ages from their mean. It describes age-label dispersion rather than prediction error.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Current performance-first ElasticNet fits
claim_text: The current Fig. 2E,F and the model-fit elements in Fig. 2A use the subsequent performance-first ElasticNet source models with 750 fibroblast and 350 endothelial Celltype_Gene features. Applied to the development data used for fitting, these models achieved R² 0.950 and 0.950, MAE 4.98 and 5.03 years, and median absolute error 3.66 and 3.50 years, respectively (Table 1). Each plotted point represents one development sample; the displayed 640 and 437 observations are in-sample predictions. These panels do not establish out-of-fold performance of the compact feature sets.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Current performance-first ElasticNet fits
claim_text: The adapted performance-first models were evaluated on 93 fibroblast and 77 endothelial external samples, yielding R² 0.377 and 0.391, MAE 8.71 and 9.28 years, and median absolute error 4.69 and 6.42 years. These are the values in the lower external panels of Fig. 2A. The ALL100 designation identifies all eligible external observations rather than a literal sample count of one hundred. External outcomes participated in selecting the feature representation and optimization settings, in addition to supplying labeled adaptation samples. Accordingly, these results are outcome-informed external-cohort performance, not independent external validation.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Current performance-first ElasticNet fits
claim_text: Even the reused 70% subset was involved in ALL100-based model selection. Its R² of 0.032 for fibroblasts and 0.043 for endothelial cells therefore remains selection-affected. In contrast to panel D, MAD in the current model-fit and external panels denotes median absolute prediction error, here reported as MedAE. This difference in metric definitions is retained explicitly rather than assigning one meaning to all MAD labels.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Protocol-specific evidence for the transfer gap
claim_text: An earlier unreduced ElasticNet branch provides a separate comparison of transfer before and after adaptation. It used 20,000 fibroblast and 10,000 endothelial features, selected after the family-specific benchmark, and achieved conditional five-fold validation R² of 0.742 and 0.633 with MAE 11.86 and 14.18 years. Without adaptation, the full-development models yielded external R² −2.943 and −1.720 and MAE 29.32 and 24.89 years in 93 and 77 samples. Negative R² indicates worse squared-error prediction than the mean of the corresponding external age labels.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Protocol-specific evidence for the transfer gap
claim_text: For that earlier branch, adaptation used 28 fibroblast and 23 endothelial samples, leaving 65 and 54 group-disjoint samples for evaluation. On matched held-out observations, MAE fell from 29.02 to 13.14 years for fibroblasts and from 25.65 to 13.18 years for endothelial cells, while adapted R² remained −0.001 and −0.355. These results document a substantial transfer gap despite reduced error after target-cohort refitting. They are not the validation results of the current 750/350-feature models. Alternate integrations of the same external samples and per-GSE representations are likewise not independent biological replications.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Cellular senescence scores answer a distinct question
claim_text: The supporting CellAge snapshot contained hUSI scores for 1,665,482 fibroblast-lineage and 536,017 endothelial-lineage cells, with SenCID identity recommendations available for 1,372,858 and 352,228 cells. hUSI represents senescence-associated transcription rather than age in years [7]. The available recSID dimensions characterize senescence identities and cannot substitute for genuine SenCID senescence-intensity outputs [8]. Dataset-wise score normalization also limits interpretation of absolute cross-dataset or cross-lineage differences.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Cellular senescence scores answer a distinct question
claim_text: The historical snapshot used an older, partially evaluated clock branch, so its clock–score associations cannot validate the current performance-first models. We therefore aligned the current selected cell states to the adult ModelFeature_CellAge analysis reported in Results Part 3 and Fig. 6. That analysis distinguishes within-sample relative hUSI from within-state age associations and composition changes. A complete evaluation linking current-model out-of-fold predictions or independently validated age acceleration to senescence scores remains unavailable.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Performance-first features span multiple stromal states
claim_text: Downstream analyses used the current performance-first representation: 750 fibroblast Celltype_Gene pairs encoding 678 unique genes and 350 endothelial pairs encoding 337 genes, spanning 27 detailed states per lineage (Fig. 3A,B). Selected features combined global and celltype-balanced candidate sources with recorded bootstrap denominators of 1,500. Their minimum retained selection frequencies were 0.600 and 0.602. These sets differ from the earlier 300-bootstrap, frequency-0.70 interpretation branch and were not interchanged with it. The current gene sets shared 45 genes, leaving 633 fibroblast-only and 292 endothelial-only memberships; these membership differences do not establish intrinsic lineage specificity.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Performance-first features span multiple stromal states
claim_text: Feature counts were uneven across states. eFibro_COL1A1_pan contributed 70 fibroblast pairs, followed by Myfibro_CALD1_pan with 65 and qFibro_CLU_pan with 62. VenEC_CLU_eye contributed 64 endothelial pairs, followed by EndoMT_VIM_pan with 37 and ArtEC_FLT1_pan with 35. Counts describe representation within the selected model, not cell abundance, independently tested subtype importance or evidence of a lineage transition. Because external outcomes influenced model selection, these downstream annotations are exploratory descriptions of the selected predictors.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Performance-first features span multiple stromal states
claim_text: Expression-pattern displays retained 520 fibroblast and 161 endothelial features after coverage and dynamic-range filtering (Fig. 3C,D). Of the fibroblast features, 183, 43 and 294 had their highest display-window mean in the source-defined young, middle and old windows; the corresponding endothelial counts were 34, 21 and 106. These windows group original A–H labels for visualization and do not establish equal-width chronological-age intervals. Display filtering and row scaling are not differential-expression tests. Likewise, a positive or negative ElasticNet coefficient is a conditional predictive weight, not a demonstrated pro-aging or anti-aging effect.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Functional annotation distinguishes lineage-associated themes
claim_text: Functional analysis used measured lineage-specific backgrounds of 11,700 fibroblast and 11,521 endothelial genes and complete library-specific correction families (Fig. 3E–J). In fibroblasts, all selected genes were enriched for the Hallmark inflammatory response (18 overlapping genes; BH q = 0.0185), TNFα signaling via NF-κB (20 genes; q = 0.0339) and the collagen-containing extracellular matrix cellular-component term (26 genes; q = 0.0269). These overlaps connect predictive features to inflammatory and matrix-associated annotations without demonstrating pathway activation or its cause.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Functional annotation distinguishes lineage-associated themes
claim_text: The endothelial set was enriched for cytoskeleton (30 genes; q = 0.0194), KEGG mineral absorption (seven genes; q = 0.00791) and the Reactome 2022 metallothionein metal-binding term (four genes; q = 0.0183). The latter overlap comprised MT1E, MT1M, MT1X and MT2A and also contributed to related metal-response annotations. Such overlapping terms are not independent replications and do not establish exposure to a particular metal. The current main network uses Reactome 2022; separate older signed-feature outputs using Reactome 2024 were not merged into this correction family.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Functional annotation distinguishes lineage-associated themes
claim_text: Gene–theme networks summarized significant memberships rather than inferred causal interactions. A separate KEGG context display showed 28 fibroblast pathways covering 132 genes and 25 endothelial pathways covering 52 genes (Extended Data Fig. 3). Inclusion in that display did not require every row to be significant; the fibroblast global all-gene KEGG analysis had no FDR-significant term. Theme membership and selected network edges therefore serve as annotation aids rather than additional statistical discoveries.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Regulator inference identifies candidates with limited adult age support
claim_text: LISA2 analysis integrated public chromatin information with selected gene sets for 14 of 27 fibroblast states and five of 27 endothelial states (Fig. 4A–C). Other states lacked sufficient mapped input genes and were retained as unavailable. After accounting for the number of ChIP datasets per factor and correcting across all factor–state tests within each lineage, examples included TP53 in Myfibro_TUBB2B_pan (q = 7.51 × 10⁻⁷), SOX4 in eFibro_COL1A1_pan (q = 8.44 × 10⁻⁸) and TEAD1 in Myfibro_TAGLN_pan (q = 0.0123). Endothelial candidates included HSF1 in EndoMT_PTN_pan (q = 1.78 × 10⁻¹²), SMARCC1 in ArtEC_FLT1_brain (q = 0.000146) and RUNX1T1 in EndoMT_VIM_pan (q = 0.00186). These results indicate regulatory association with the input gene set; they do not establish factor activation with age or direct binding in the sampled stromal cells.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Regulator inference identifies candidates with limited adult age support
claim_text: A separate CollecTRI-prior-constrained RNA analysis was evaluable in 21 fibroblast and 15 endothelial states. It tested 352,675 and 241,986 candidate edges and retained 13,994 and 4,747 supported edges, including 65 and seven edges whose targets matched selected Celltype_Gene features (Fig. 4D,E). These are edge counts rather than unique target-gene counts. Their interpretation depends on prior knowledge, covariate adjustment, sign concordance and resampling support. A stricter adult within-cohort sensitivity analysis tested 1,434 fibroblast and 1,054 endothelial factor–state associations; none survived lineage-wide BH correction. Thus, the network candidates were not established as general adult age-associated regulators.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Adult raw-count analysis reveals tissue-dependent matrix-associated contrasts
claim_text: To examine matrix-associated transcription in adults, raw counts were aggregated within training-sample proxies and selected states after age-concordance and coverage filtering. The analysis retained 300,431 fibroblast cells in 1,748 proxy-by-state pseudobulks and 166,664 endothelial cells in 905 pseudobulks. Counts with fractional entries were not rounded; noninteger genes were excluded separately for each fitted profile. Negative-binomial aged-versus-young models were estimable for 39 cell-state or cell-state-by-tissue profiles (Fig. 5A–D). AGRN was the only shared selected ECM-associated gene, a membership observation rather than a replicated age effect.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Adult raw-count analysis reveals tissue-dependent matrix-associated contrasts
claim_text: Using full-gene Wald statistics as inputs to signed gene-set regression, 67 of 312 ECM-signature comparisons met FDR ≤ 0.05 after correction across both lineages: 41 fibroblast and 26 endothelial comparisons. These include overlapping signatures and analysis scopes and are not 67 independent biological replications. For eFibro_COL1A1_pan, the collagen-formation signature had a negative contrast in ovary (ULM score −5.81; q = 1.03 × 10⁻⁶; eight sample proxies), whereas ECM organization had a positive contrast in colon (+4.65; q = 0.000116; eleven proxies). ArtEC_FLT1_pan in adipose showed a positive collagen-formation contrast (+5.33; q = 7.98 × 10⁻⁶; twelve proxies). Each example arose from one study, and these separate contrasts are not a formal age-by-tissue interaction test.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Adult raw-count analysis reveals tissue-dependent matrix-associated contrasts
claim_text: Among 142 displayed mechanosensitive-regulator comparisons, only TEAD4 in adipose ArtEC_FLT1_pan survived correction across the full 22,346-test transcription-factor family (ULM score +3.95; q = 0.0174; seven younger and five older proxies from one study; Fig. 5E). The results therefore do not support a general claim of YAP/TAZ–TEAD activation across stromal states. At the exact selected-feature level, PLA2G4A in ovary eFibro_COL1A1_pan was the sole significant ECM-associated example (aged-versus-young log₂ fold change 2.60; cross-profile q = 0.0132; Table 2). No endothelial exact-feature association passed that correction. No same-state candidate simultaneously satisfied the LISA2, TF-age and target-gene-age significance criteria in the integrated candidate table. The broader heatmaps in Fig. 5F,G instead summarize globally selected ECM-associated genes across cell-state-level profiles and do not establish exact-feature support in every displayed state.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Selected cellular states differ in relative senescence-associated transcription
claim_text: The current ModelFeature_CellAge analysis aligned the 27 selected states per lineage to adult, age-concordant samples, encompassing 731 fibroblast sample proxies from 87 studies and 529 endothelial proxies from 80 studies before state-specific primary coverage requirements (Fig. 6). The primary within-sample comparison estimated each state's mean hUSI difference from the cell-weighted mean of other scored cells in the same lineage and sample-by-tissue unit. Seventeen fibroblast and fourteen endothelial states had estimable relative-score contrasts; seven and eight, respectively, survived correction across both lineages within this metric.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Selected cellular states differ in relative senescence-associated transcription
claim_text: Fibroblast eFibro_COL1A2_pan showed a positive relative hUSI difference of 0.0315 (95% CI, 0.0216–0.0414; q = 1.29 × 10⁻⁶; 185 sample proxies across 45 studies), as did Myfibro_CALD1_pan (0.0287; 0.0186–0.0388; q = 1.46 × 10⁻⁵; 134 proxies across 34 studies). Endothelial VenEC_CLU_pan showed a negative difference (−0.0166; −0.0237 to −0.00955; q = 0.000218; 125 proxies across 34 studies). These three directions remained significant in healthy-only, training-only, outside-training and alternate cell-threshold sensitivity analyses. Those analyses reuse overlapping observations and are sensitivity checks rather than independent replication.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained

heading: Selected cellular states differ in relative senescence-associated transcription
claim_text: No primary adjusted within-state hUSI–age, younger-versus-older hUSI, SSE-fraction or composition–age comparison survived its metric-specific correction. In particular, continuous hUSI–age models were estimable for sixteen fibroblast and thirteen endothelial states, with no FDR-significant slope. Model feature count and coefficient-derived importance also showed no FDR-significant exploratory correlation with the tested CellAge summaries. Moreover, 553 of 678 fibroblast selected genes and 276 of 337 endothelial genes overlapped the hUSI signature. Relative hUSI therefore describes a dependent transcriptomic state contrast, not independent validation of the clock or evidence that a selected cell state ages faster.
status: source-verified; protocol and exploratory limits retained
